finding.title: Override localDayClockProvider in track_detail_screen_test.dart to remove its wall-clock dependency

evidence.quote:
userDatabaseProvider.overrideWith((ref) => db),
    // Goal writes go through goalRepositoryProvider,

finding.why: TrackDetailScreen reads localDayClockProvider via _trackPaceCalcProvider (default = SystemLocalDayClock, real DateTime.now()). track_detail_screen_test.dart's _overridesFor list never overrides it, while every sibling file that mounts the same screen in this batch (track_detail_goal_stale_test.dart, edit_track_and_detail_l1_test.dart) does, with FakeLocalDayClock pinned to 2026-05-30. No current assertion in track_detail_screen_test.dart depends on paceCalc's output, so this isn't flaky today, but it's one inconsistent override away from date-dependent flakiness the moment someone adds an assertion that touches TrackInfoCard's pace-derived text (days-remaining, projected finish), and it's inconsistent with the established pattern in the same directory.
finding.recommendation: Add localDayClockProvider.overrideWithValue(FakeLocalDayClock(DateTime.utc(2026, 5, 30))) (or another fixed date) to _overridesFor, matching the sibling files.
acceptance_criteria: track_detail_screen_test.dart's _overridesFor includes a localDayClockProvider override with a fixed date

finding.title: Rewrite TrackLearningOrderScreen 'race-safety' test to actually verify the _sedarimSaveSeq guard
finding.rule: TQ-8 (regression test weaker than what the source can do wrong) / Feathers seam lens
finding.why: Test '20. rapid successive reorders only persist the final order (seq guard)' claims to pin the _sedarimSaveSeq race guard, but its only assertions are that saveSedarimOrder was called twice and that some DraggableOrderItem still renders. Both saves are dispatched regardless of the guard (the guard only gates the *post-await* provider-invalidate/setState in _persistSedarim), so deleting the 'mySeq != _sedarimSaveSeq' checks entirely would not change either assertion's outcome — the test cannot fail if the guard regresses. Contrast with track_learning_order_reset_test.dart in the same batch, which correctly uses controlled Completers to prove which read 'wins'; that pattern is available and not applied here, so a future refactor could silently reintroduce the stale-continuation race (flicker/revert of the reordered list) with CI green.
finding.recommendation: Give the mocked repo.saveSedarimOrder two distinguishable outcomes (e.g. via Completers, as done in track_learning_order_reset_test.dart) so the first (slow) save's post-await continuation would visibly corrupt state if it ran; assert that only the second reorder's masechtos invalidation/refetch is reflected in the rendered order, and that the test fails when the mySeq guard is removed.
acceptance_criteria: Test fails (red) when the 'if (!mounted || mySeq != _sedarimSaveSeq) return;' guard is deleted from _persistSedarim in track_learning_order_screen.dart
Test distinguishes stale vs fresh masechtos-fetch results (e.g. per-call Completers) rather than only counting saveSedarimOrder invocations
Final rendered/persisted order is asserted to match the second (last) reorder, not merely 'a list renders without crashing'

finding.title: Fix clear_overdue_button_test.dart's push-spy test to verify SyncWriteFacade, the collaborator EditTrackScreen actually calls
finding.rule: Feathers seam lens / TQ-8 (does the test exercise the real production code path?)
finding.why: edit_track_screen.dart never imports or touches FirestoreGateway (grep confirms only sync_providers.dart is imported); its real _clearOverdue() calls SyncWriteFacade.pushProfileProgram(Map payload) — a single-arg interface that for non-tutored profiles is enqueued to the outbox (OutboxSyncWriteFacade.pushProfileProgram -> enqueueProfileProgram) and only reaches FirestoreGateway.pushProfileProgram(profileId:, data:) two layers later, asynchronously, via PushPipelineImpl. Test E instead hand-builds a parallel 'reanchorProgramTrack' helper (explicitly documented as 'mirrors the logic in edit_track_screen.dart's _clearOverdue() ... extracted here') that calls a mocked FirestoreGateway directly with named params. This is the ONLY test in the repo referencing _clearOverdue/clearOverdue (grep -rl over test/ returns just this file), so it is the sole regression coverage for the F-C1 fix (a documented past bug: the push to Firestore was missing). The helper's copy has already drifted from production — the real payload includes 'updated_at' (edit_track_screen.dart:394) but the test's reimplemented payload and its assertions omit that key entirely — proving the duplication is not being kept in sync. If _clearOverdue stops calling syncFacade?.pushProfileProgram, calls the wrong facade, or drops a payload field, this test suite stays green.
finding.recommendation: Drive the real EditTrackScreen widget (pump + tap the Clear Overdue button + confirm dialog) with syncWriteFacadeProvider overridden to a mock/fake SyncWriteFacade, and assert on the Map payload SyncWriteFacade.pushProfileProgram receives (including updated_at) instead of hand-mocking FirestoreGateway from a reimplemented helper.
acceptance_criteria: Test fails (red) if edit_track_screen.dart's _clearOverdue() stops calling syncWriteFacadeProvider/pushProfileProgram
Test asserts the actual SyncWriteFacade.pushProfileProgram(Map) interface, not FirestoreGateway.pushProfileProgram(profileId:, data:)
Payload assertion includes every key the production code sends (profile_id, curriculum_id, program_id, tracking_start_date, tracking_start_ref, updated_at)

finding.title: Close every inMemoryDb() Drift database opened by tracks/setup and track_order widget tests
finding.rule: TQ-6 (hermetic tests / no shared/leaked state) — violates drift_memory.dart's own documented contract

evidence.quote:
/// Callers MUST `await db.close()` in `tearDown` to free the native
/// resources.

finding.why: drift_memory.dart's own doc comment says callers MUST close every inMemoryDb() in tearDown to free native FFI/sqlite3 resources. step_starting_position_l1_test.dart creates 6 in-memory DBs (lines 222, 234, 251, 1017, 1075, 1127) and closes none. track_management_body_and_order_l1_test.dart creates 8 and closes only 3 (the other 5 — lines 158, 204, 304, 461, 929 — leak once per test invocation that hits them, i.e. ~13+ leaked native handles across that file's test run). track_management_hub_screen_l1_test.dart's shared default at line 120 leaks once per test that doesn't pass an explicit db (~10 tests). track_learning_order_reset_test.dart's single DB is never closed. Across a full CI run this accumulates open native sqlite3 handles per test file, risking slow teardown/fd pressure and contradicts the helper's explicit contract.
finding.recommendation: Add `addTearDown(() => database.close())` (or an explicit `await db.close()`) immediately after every inMemoryDb() call site listed, including the shared `db ?? inMemoryDb()` defaults in _buildBodyApp/_buildApp/_buildStartingPositionApp-style helpers.
acceptance_criteria: Every inMemoryDb() call in the 4 listed files is paired with a db.close() (or addTearDown close) reachable on both pass and fail paths
A Rule-0 grep/lint (e.g. compare inMemoryDb() count vs close()/addTearDown-close count per test file) fails CI when the counts diverge

finding.title: Split tracks/setup test files that exceed AG-3's 400-line cap
finding.why: step_starting_position_l1_test.dart is 1510 lines and its own header admits it covers three separate widgets (StartingPositionStep, StartingPositionCalendarMode, SelfPacedGoalStep) that live in three separate lib files; track_management_body_and_order_l1_test.dart is 1089 lines covering two unrelated screens (TrackManagementBody and TrackLearningOrderScreen) in two different lib directories. Bundling unrelated widgets into one file means every unrelated change re-runs/re-reviews the whole file, and AG-5 mirroring is already broken for these (no single lib file maps 1:1 to them).
finding.recommendation: Split each along AG-5 mirrored-path boundaries: one test file per lib source file under test (e.g. step_starting_position_l1_test.dart -> step_starting_position_test.dart + step_starting_position_calendar_test.dart + step_goal_test.dart), each landing under 400 lines.
acceptance_criteria: Each resulting test file is ≤400 lines and covers exactly one mirrored lib source file
make audit (or a new AG-3 line-count checker) reports zero violators in this directory
